dedupe_keys.name: crop insurance losses by climatic damage cause in the inland pacific northwest 2001 to 2022

description: This dataset supports an analysis of how climate-related damage causes drive crop insurance losses across 24 counties of the inland Pacific Northwest of the United States. It was produced by Erich Seamon, Paul Gessler and Stephen Lee of the University of Idaho, John Abatzoglou of the University of California, Merced, and Philip Mote of Oregon State University, and published on Dryad in 2023. Drawing on the US Department of Agriculture's 2.8 million record national claims data, it covers more than 31,000 loss claims from 2001 to 2022. Wheat dominates losses with over 2.8 billion dollars in indemnities, 1.5 billion of them from drought, while fruit losses of about 400 million dollars come mainly from freeze, frost and hail. The authors used principal components analysis to separate spatial and temporal patterns by damage cause for wheat and apples. The files, about 512 MB, are free to download from Dryad under a Creative Commons Zero public domain dedication. Caveats: insured losses reflect policy uptake and rules, not total crop damage. Simulation uses: hazard-specific agricultural loss rates for food production shock and climate adaptation models. Related records: the USDA RMA cause of loss data (data-usda-rma-cause-of-loss) are the national source.
